title: Whole text: glyph habits that depend on the line position and on the previous word's last glyph, plus page-local copying
statement: Five components, each something a scribe could do without meaning: spell glyph by glyph with a habit that differs for the first, last and inner words of a line (order 4); spell with a habit that depends on the last glyph of the word just written (order 4); copy a word from the last 50 on the page, exactly or with one glyph changed; and plain glyph trigrams as the fallback. Chosen on the public practice split only, by comparing ten mixtures. There the mixture scores 11.003 bits per word, 0.583 below the bag of words, against 0.342 for the earlier best kind of mixture (glyph trigrams, copying, line-position vocabulary and prefix templates, as in M-003). Ablations on the same split: adding only the previous-glyph speller (order 3) to that earlier mixture gains 0.464, only the line-position speller 0.478, both 0.554; order 4 for both 0.583; order 5 is worse (0.551). With both spellers in, the line-position vocabulary, the prefix templates and the word-to-word chain add nothing measurable (under 0.001 bits per word), so they are left out. Reading: most of what line position and the previous word tell about the next word is carried by glyphs at the word's edges, not by which word it is, in line with F-001, F-002 and F-006. The score is conditional on the line breaks (the model is told whether a word is first, last or inside its line). Fitted weights on practice: line-position speller 0.45, previous-glyph speller 0.29, trigrams 0.19, exact copy 0.055, altered copy 0.013.
